Consult Summary:
28-year-old woman with no prior headache history presents via teleconsult with a new, left-posterior throbbing headache since yesterday; no red-flag features; advised trial of stronger NSAID and paracetamol, rest, hydration, and safety-net instructions.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Headache.  
  – Onset: Yesterday mid-morning (≈24 hrs ago).  
  – Location: Left occipital region.  
  – Character: Intense, throbbing.  
  – Severity: 8/10.  
  – Course: Gradually built up; persistent; no diurnal variation.  
  – Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not affected by position, coughing, bending. Ibuprofen (Nurofen) provided little relief.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies nausea, vomiting, visual changes, photophobia, phonophobia, limb weakness, numbness, tingling, fever, chills, sweats, rash, neck stiffness. Appetite/fluids normal.  
• Prior occurrence: No previous headaches.  
• Functional impact: Difficult to concentrate on work but has not missed work.  
• Systems review: otherwise unremarkable.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.

Medications:
• Ibuprofen (Nurofen) – dose/route/frequency not documented; single dose taken yesterday.
• No regular prescription medications.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies reported.

Social History:
• Lives with partner.  
• Occupation: Designer.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Denies regular use.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
• Mother: Hypertension; migraines.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – video/telephone consultation; no vitals available.)

Investigations:
• None performed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: New unilateral occipital headache, likely primary tension-type or migraine without aura.  
  – Trial stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) in place of ibuprofen; take with food.  
  – May alternate/augment with paracetamol as needed.  
  – Encourage rest, adequate hydration.  
  – Safety-net: Seek urgent review if headache worsens, persists >1–2 days despite therapy, or if new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, visual or neurological deficits, recurrent episodes).  
  – Re-contact clinic if concerns; consider in-person assessment and blood pressure measurement if symptoms persist.

General Plan items:
• None.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Vitals, objective neurological exam, blood pressure, full medication list confirmation, allergy confirmation (only “no” given).  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational fillers removed.
